features.name: Mathematical Casting
features.text:
Mathematics is the fundament by which the arithmetician quantifies everything including magic. Each day he can use this ability a number of times equal to half his arithmetician level (minimum 1) plus his Intelligence modifier, the arithmetician can cause his spell to tap into the fundamental mathematics of reality. This is a free action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. 
The arithmetician gains one “Parameter” at 1st level and every four levels thereafter to a maximum of 5. Parameters are countable aspects of reality that can be found in combat-based scenarios. Some examples are [Initiative, Strength Score, Base Attack Bonus, missing Hit Point or even Number of Limbs]. No matter what the choice, it must be something that every person in combat would potentially have a number for.
Also, at 1st level and every six levels thereafter, the arithmetician gains a new “Number”. He must choose one of the following:
• Three
• Four
• Five
• Any Prime Number 7 or higher 
These numbers will select the targets of the arithmetician’s mathematically altered spell. By selecting one Parameter he knows and one Number he knows, the spell the arithmetician now casts affects everyone (ally, enemy and himself) within the spell’s range that has that Parameter at a number evenly divisible by the Number he chose. 
Ex. If one chose limbs and 4 for his spell, it would affect all party members that have 2 arms and 2 legs, as well as the spider they are facing that has 8 legs (creatures that have 0 of the given parameter, such as an ooze with 0 limbs, are unaffected).

features.name: Arithmetic
features.text: At 2nd level, an arithmetician can solve any mathematical equation almost instantly. He gains the ability to solve any mathematical problem as a free action. In addition, his analytical mind quickly accesses situations, allowing him to act while others are still debating the appropriate courses of action. The arithmetician may add his Intelligence modifier in addition to his Dexterity modifier to his initiative rolls.

features.name: Magical Foundations
features.text: At 2nd level, an arithmetician receives a +1 bonus on all Spellcraft and Use Magic Device checks. This bonus increases by +1 every other level thereafter, to a maximum of a +10 bonus at 20th level.

features.name: Numerical Talents (Ex or Su)
features.text:
As an arithmetician gains experience, he learns a number of talents that assist him in manipulating spells and other forms of magic. At 2nd level and every two levels thereafter, the arithmetician gains one Numerical talent. An arithmetician cannot select an individual talent more than once. Talents marked with an asterisk add effects to an arithmetician’s spellcasting ability. Only one of these talents can be applied to an individual spell and the decision must be made before the spell is cast.
• A complete list of numerical talents can be found here: Numerical Talents

features.name: Magical Theorem
features.text:
At 3rd level and every other level thereafter, the arithmetician learns how to apply one type of mathematics to his spells. Magical theorems are divided into five disciplines (Algebra, Geometry, Calculus, Topology, and Statistics). The first magical theorem in each discipline may be learned by any arithmetician, but subsequent theorems may only be learned once the preceding theorems in the discipline have been mastered.
Algebra
• Subtraction: The arithmetician simply subtracts energy from the sum total of what is required to alter his spells. When applying a metamagic feat to a spell he casts, he subtracts 1 MP the metamagic feat imposes upon the spell (which also reduces the spell level of the spell) to a minimum of 1.
• Addition: The arithmetician adds additional energy to his spells, rendering them more effective. He adds one to each dice of variable numbers in the spell’s description.
• Equation: By mastering algebra, the arithmetician gains the ability to link two creatures together in an equation. As a standard action, he may designate two creatures, who each receive a Will save (DC 10 + half of the arithmetician’s level + his Intelligence modifier). If both creatures fail their saving throw, they are linked together for one round per class level the arithmetician possesses. If one of the linked creatures takes damage, loses hit points, heals damage, or suffers a status effect, the other creature is affected as well, suffering the same effects, taking the same amount of damage, or healing the same amount of hit points. If one of the linked creatures dies, the remaining creature must immediately succeed at a Fortitude save against this ability’s DC or die. If one of the creatures is immune to a form of damage or a status effect, both creatures are immune.
Geometry
• Euclidean Space: The arithmetician gains a better understanding of distances and spatial relations. He adds 5 feet for every two levels of the arithmetician class he possesses to the range of each of his non-Touch spells.
• Riemann Manifolds: The arithmetician’s understanding of geometry is such that he is able to curve his spells around obstacles. When casting any spell requiring a ranged touch attack, the arithmetician can ignore any benefit the target gains from cover, and never risks harming an ally in melee or grappling with a target.
• Lobachevskian Dimensions: The arithmetician understands the curvature of the multiverse and can warp it, allowing him to reach his target from safety. He may cast any of his “Touch” range spells as if they had a range of “Close,” though doing so requires a ranged touch attack rather than a melee touch attack.
Calculus
• Integrals: The arithmetician can integrate his spells, making them more cohesive and difficult to break down. The DC to dispel an arithmetician’s spells increases by +4.
• Derivatives: The arithmetician can differentiate his spells, allowing them to function in non-continuous units of time. After a spell is cast, the arithmetician can choose to differentiate his spell as a move action, causing the spell to become suspended. While suspended, duration does not elapse for the spell. He may recall his spell as a move action, at which point it continues from the point at which it had been differentiated. The arithmetician may differentiate each spell only once. 
• Time Variance: The arithmetician understands how time functions and can break down spells cast upon him. When a spell is cast on the arithmetician, as an immediate action he can halve or increase by half the duration of the spell.
Topology
• Manifolds: The arithmetician can create complex figures by combining copies of similar figures. When determining the area of any shapeable spell, the arithmetician increases the area by one half (+50%).
• Homeomorphism: The arithmetician learns how to transform variables from one set to another set while still preserving the values of the original. He may alter any area-affecting spell he casts so that it affects an area different from its normal area, as selected from the following list: Cylinder (10-foot radius, 30 feet high), Cone (40 feet long), Cubes (four 10-foot cubes), or a sphere (20-foot radius spread). The spell works otherwise normally in all respects.
• Knot Theory: The arithmetician understands mathematical knots, allowing him to twist, tangle, and shape his area effect spells. The arithmetician can alter any of his area effect spells so that they exclude any square or squares within their area of effect, as determined by him.
Statistics
• Above Average: The arithmetician learns to skew the law of averages, and may take 11 on any action on which he would normally be able to take 10. In addition, he may choose to take 11 on caster level checks, including Concentration checks, dispel checks and checks made to overcome spell resistance.
• Eschew Dice: Whenever the arithmetician casts a spell with variable effects, he may choose to take the average on each dice instead of rolling (d3 = 2, d4 = 3, d6 = 4, d8 = 5, d10 = 6, d12 = 7).
• Outliers: The arithmetician learns that occasional values are created which exist beyond the accepted range of results, and manipulates such values to his benefit. For a number of times per day equal to the arithmetician’s Intelligence modifier, he gains a +20 on a single skill check or caster level check he makes.

features.name: Clear Mind
features.text: At 5th level, an arithmetician can regain his MP quicker. The arithmetician must be relaxed and must be free from overt distractions, such as combat raging nearby or other loud noises. For example, he could be riding in the back of a carriage and benefit from this ability. The arithmetician does not gain this recovery if he is asleep or unconscious. The arithmetician regains 1 MP per hour. This increases by 1 for every five arithmetician levels after 5th.

features.name: Targeted Mathematics
features.text: At 7th level, as a swift action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity, the arithmetician chooses one creature he can see. He selects one Parameter and Number he knows, if the Parameter is a number evenly divisible by the Number he chose for the creature, all spells he casts that only target that creature gain the same discount that Flexible Spellcasting provides his memorized spells. This effect lasts for one minute, or until you use this feature again. The arithmetician can use this ability a number of times per day equal to his Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Cup of Life
features.text: At 9th level, the arithmetician can make sure that nothing in the equation goes to waste. Whenever an arithmetician casts a spell that heals damage, if it puts himself or an ally over their max, the remaining HP is given to the next closest ally, within 30 feet, that isn’t at full HP. So long as there is extra HP remaining you can continue to do this until there are no extra targets.

features.name: Split
features.text: At 11th level, an arithmetician sees incoming spells as numbers and with just a thought, can split the numbers in half and transfer them to other people, including the original caster. As an immediate action when targeted by a spell, the arithmetician can make a Spellcraft check (DC 15 + double the spell’s level), if successful, the spell’s healing or damage is halved, now targeting an additional creature within range of the original spell for the same amount. Any spell that requires an attack roll that hits the arithmetician will automatically hit his intended target. Any saving throws required will be based on the caster who cast the spell. The arithmetician can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + his Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Drop Remainder
features.text:
At 13th level, when an arithmetician witnesses an effect that damages or causes death to any number of creatures, as an immediate action, he may spare those so weak to be negligible in a fight. Any creature that their hit die is both less than his own and 10 or more less than the creature causing the effect (assume traps and environmental effects have hit die equal to their CR) takes no damage and does not die from the effect.
Any given creature may only benefit from this ability once per day.

features.name: Mathematical Manipulations
features.text: At 17th level, as part of casting a spell an arithmetician can reduce the radius of a spread or burst effect or shorten the length of a cone. All changes must occur in 5-foot increments, to a minimum of 5 feet. Alternatively, the arithmetician can change the area of effect of a cone spell to a line with a length equal to the spell’s range. In addition, the arithmetician can bend the line of a spell that has a line area of effect up to 90 degrees at any single point along the line’s length.

features.name: Soul Bind
features.text: At 19th level, the arithmetician begins to understand that even the body can be broken down in equations and slightly altered. Whenever he takes physical damage, if it is a multiple of the ‘Number’ he knows, as an immediate action, he is healed for half (rounded down) of the damage while the attacker takes that much damage.

features.name: Axiom
features.text:
At 20th level, as a free action, an arithmetician may push the next spell he casts to the limits of reality, doubling the maximum number of components he may use for the spell, and automatically passes the Spellcraft check for casting it. He may only do this once per day.
Favored Class Bonuses
Instead of receiving an additional skill rank or hit point whenever they gain a level in a favored class, some races have the option of choosing from a number of other bonuses, depending upon their favored classes. The following options are available to the listed race who have arithmetician as their favored class, and unless otherwise stated, the bonus applies each time you select the listed favored class reward.
• Aegyl: The arithmetician gains +1/6th of a talent.
• Al Bhed: The arithmetician adds +1/3rd of an additional use of Mathematical Casting per day.
• Antica: Get a -1/5 bonus to the component cost of the Silent spell component in the Metaspell category. To a possible component cost reduction of -4 (final cost of -2) at level 20. 
• Bangaa: Add +1/4 to caster level checks made to overcome a creature’s spell resistance. 
• Dwarf: Select one item creation feat known by the arithmetician. Whenever he crafts an item using that feat, the amount of progress he makes in an 8-hour period increases by 200 gil (50 gil if crafting while adventuring). This does not reduce the cost of the item; it just increases the rate at which the item is crafted.
• Elvaan: Add +1/4 to caster level checks made to overcome a creature’s spell resistance.
• Galka: Select one item creation feat known by the arithmetician. Whenever he crafts an item using that feat, the amount of progress he makes in an 8-hour period increases by 200 gil (50 gil if crafting while adventuring). This does not reduce the cost of the item; it just increases the rate at which the item is crafted.
• Genome: Add +1/6 bonus to Knowledge (all) skill checks.
• Half-Breed: The arithmetician gains +1/6th of a talent.
• Hume: The arithmetician gains +1/6th of a talent.
• Kindred: Any elemental resistance that a creature affected by the arithmeticians spells has is considered +1/4 less when determining damage from elemental spells he casts. 
• Lambkin: Add +1/6 bonus to Knowledge (all) skill checks.
• Mandragora: Reduce Spell Exhaustion suffered by +1/6. 
• Mithra: Add +1/4 to the arithmetician’s initiative rolls.
• Moogle: Select one item creation feat known by the black mage. Whenever he crafts an item using that feat, the amount of progress he makes in an 8-hour period increases by 200 gil (50 gil if crafting while adventuring). This does not reduce the cost of the item; it just increases the rate at which the item is crafted.
• Mutant: The arithmetician gains +1/6th of a talent. 
• Nu Mou: Add +1/6 bonus to Knowledge (all) skill checks.
• Orc: The arithmetician gains +1/2 Strength. (+1 Strength every two times you select this option.) 
• PuPu: Add +1/2 bonus to Craft skill checks.
• Seeq: Add +1/5 to the arithmetician’s Fortitude saving throws.
• Shindroid: Reduce Spell Exhaustion suffered by +1/6. 
• Sylph: Reduce Spell Exhaustion suffered by +1/6. 
• Tarutaru: Add +1/2 bonus to Craft skill checks. 
• Tonkin: Add +5 feet range to the arithmetician’s Limited Telepathy racial trait.
• Vanu Vanu: The arithmetician adds +1/3rd of an additional use of Mathematical Casting per day.
• Velkk: Add +1/4 to caster level checks made to overcome a creature’s spell resistance.
• Viera: Reduce Spell Exhaustion suffered by +1/6.

features.name: Flexible Spellcasting
features.text:
Components: Components are the building blocks of spells. The number of which determines the strength of the spell. They are a measure of the spells and the Arithmeticians limits, not a resource pool. Much as an artist uses paint to create a mural or a weaver uses colored thread to create a tapestry, an arithmetician uses components to create a spell. The arithmetician creates spells by choosing the proper components to generate the outcome the arithmetician wants. Two major categories of components exist, Required Components: Area, duration and range, and Effect Components: Control, Force, Summon and more. 
Note: Just as the arithmetician spends points on different components for his spell effects, he can create a spell with multiple effects from the same component. For example, the arithmetician can create a spell that cures blindness and hit point damage at the same time (two Heal component effects), or a spell that throws an enemy around and damages them protects against fire and ice (two Force component effects). Pay for each effect separately.

features.name: Components costs, required vs effect.
features.text:
Area, Duration and range are Required Components — the arithmetician always has to know what the magic is going to affect, how long it’s going to last and how far it reaches. Add their costs together, this is the minimum the spell can cost to cast, but their components are not added to the effect components cost.
Effect components are all other component types listed below (Core, Heal, Illusion, etc.), they are what effect the spell has on what it is targeting. If the arithmetician wants to make a bandit run in fear, add a Control component. If he wants to pick the bandit up and throw him against a tree, add Force components. If the arithmetician wants to learn his darkest secrets, add a Divination component. With enough practice, the arithmetician can build a spell that does all three of these things at once, or even more. The only limits are his imagination and skill at manipulating the components of magic. When determining the cost of the spell add up the cost of all of the effect components separately from the Required Components, if they are lower than the required components then use those to determine the spells level. Otherwise, if the effect components add up to be higher than the required components total, use that value to determine the spell’s level.
Example: So, if one was to make a spell that is a 100-foot cone, originates from caster and is instantaneous, its minimum level would be 4, with a required cost of 18 components. If its only effect component was to heal all creatures in range for 1d6, its effect component cost would be 1, far lower than the minimum still making it still a 4th level spell. You would still use its minimum level of 4. but if you had it heal for 40d6 instead, then you would use its effect component cost of 40, making it a 9th level spell.

features.name: Building Spells: To build a spell, follow these steps.
features.text:
• Decide what the arithmetician wants the spell to do.
• Look at the component descriptions (below) to find which components are appropriate for his spell. 
• Add together the Area, Duration and Range components for the minimum component cost and spell level.
• Separately from required components add together the number of points the arithmetician will spend on all the effect components. If it is higher than the required component cost, use it for the spell’s component cost and spell level.
That’s it! If the arithmetician likes the spell he designed, write down its effects and component costs so he doesn’t have to build it again from scratch; doing so is especially handy for spells that he uses often, and required for memorized spells.
Steps for Spellcasting: To cast a spell, follow these steps.
On his turn, use an action appropriate to the spell’s casting time.
• Provoke an attack of opportunity from all adjacent opponents.
• Increase his current spell exhaustion by the spell’s exhaustion rating, if any.
• Spend MP according to its spell level.
• When the arithmetician finishes casting the spell, he makes a Spellcraft check (DC 10 + the component cost of the spell he is casting) to see if he successfully casts the spell. The arithmetician can take 10 on this. If the arithmetician fails this check, he fails to cast the spell. If the arithmetician succeeds, he moves to the next step.
• Apply the effects of his spell.
Note: if you are interrupted while casting a spell, whether by outside means or via your own choosing, you do not cast the spell, expend MP, or gain spell exhaustion.

features.name: Aspects of Flexible Spells
features.text:
Casting Time: By default, casting a spell is a full-round action. Certain components can speed up or slow down one’s casting time. 
Words and Gestures: All spells require verbal and somatic components. 
Attacks and Saves: A spell allows an unwilling target to resist its effects with a saving throw, and any spell that targets individual creatures makes either a melee or ranged touch attack as well. A spell’s save DC is equal to 10 + the spell level + his Intelligence modifier. Choose the save type when you build the spell. All creatures can choose to fail their save against an arithmetician’s spells. 
Schools: All spells an arithmetician casts fall into at least one, if not multiple spell schools. Some components will list in parentheses what schools and subschools are usually appropriate (such as mind-affecting for all components listed under Control), but there will be plenty of times where they won’t, so it is up to the arithmeticians with DM’s approval to choose what schools and subschools a spell is.

features.name: Spell Exhaustion
features.text:
While others stick to tried and tested spells, Arithmeticians manipulate reality on a fundamental level without normal limitations, this unique way of casting is both physically and mentally taxing. When the arithmetician successfully casts a spell, take its component cost and subtract twice his arithmetician level + the arithmeticians Constitution modifier [lvl * 2 + Con] (treating results less than 0 as 0). This number is the spell’s exhaustion rating (SE). Every time the arithmetician casts a spell, add its spell exhaustion rating (if any) to his current spell exhaustion and take non-lethal damage equal to the amount gained. For example, after casting three spells with SE 5, his spell exhaustion is 15. A fifth-level arithmetician with a +4 constitution modifier can cast three 14-point spells in a row without penalty as each one has an spell exhaustion rating of 0 (14 – 14 = 0), whereas two 18-point spells (SE 4 each) put him at a spell exhaustion of 8.
Whenever you would recover MP, if you have any points of spell exhaustion you reduce your spell exhaustion by that amount instead, only regaining MP after your spell exhaustion has been reduced to 0.
Note: Overflow is regained, if you would gain 5 MP and have 1 SE, you reduce your SE to 0 and regain 4 MP.
Averting Spell Disruption: When the arithmetician is casting a spell, taking damage forces him to make a Concentration check to cast the spell. If the arithmetician fails the check, his spell is disrupted, and he stops casting. The arithmetician does not lose any MP or increase his spell exhaustion rating for a disrupted spell.
Ending Spellcasting: The arithmetician may interrupt his own spellcasting at any time. Doing so does not take an action (he can even do it when it is not his turn), cost MP or add to his spell exhaustion rating. In effect, ending a spell is totally “free.”
Dismissing Spells: The arithmetician may end one of his ongoing spells at any time as a standard action. Doing so does not cost MP, increase his spell exhaustion rating or provoke attacks of opportunity. The arithmetician may dismiss a spell at any range.

features.name: Component Summary:
features.text:
This section gives detailed explanations of the sorts of things each component can do when added to a spell. These are examples and are by no means comprehensive lists of what each component can do — that would be impossible and work against the goal of the flexible spellcasting system. If the arithmetician wants to create a spell and the exact effect he is looking for isn’t described here, use these effects as guidelines for how many component points his spell should cost and work with your DM. The following summaries include rules clarifications for certain components.
Required Components:
Area: Determines how many creatures or how much space the spell affects.
Range: Determines the distance that the spell affects, and where its origin point is. 
Duration: Determines how long the spell lasts. The Duration refers only to ongoing magical effects, as the consequences of these effects may last much longer than the spell. For spells with a duration longer than 1 round per level, it is recommended to use the next shorter time increment when determining recurring effects. (For a damage over time spell that’s duration is measured in days, the damage recurs every hour, not every round.) 
Effect Components:
Core: These components are core aspects of a spell, how potent it is, how taxing it is to cast, how long it will take to cast.
Control: This component covers mind control and emotions. 
Divination: This component reveals or conceals information. Information revealed by a spell is accurate, but may become inaccurate. Future circumstances may change, and knowledge of the future makes such a change even more likely (for example, intervening if one knows a friend is going to die within the hour); divination spells determine the most likely outcome based on current circumstances.
Enhance: This component improves qualities of its target, even to the point of being permanent inherent bonuses. Some components can grant a creature new powers beyond their normal capabilities. 
Force: These components inflict the arithmeticians’ will upon reality with force. They can move, damage, or negate certain aspects of the world around the arithmetician. By default, a spell deals bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage. Damage reduction affects this sort of damage. The damage a spell does can be changed to be non-lethal, non-elemental, or to an energy type. Common energy types are earth, fire, holy, ice, lightning, shadow, water, and wind damage. Spells made with energy types count as being of the appropriate school type (for example, a spell that deals fire damage would be of the elemental (fire) school.)
Heal: This component heals injuries and other afflictions.
Illusion: This component creates false images and sensations. Illusions appear real but do not exert force, though the arithmetician can compensate for this drawback with other components. (For example, the arithmetician can create an illusionary beast coupled with Force components so that it can affect the world around it.) A witness to an illusion gets a save only if he interacts with it in such a way to suggest it is unreal, such as by touching or passing through the illusion. A witness who makes this save realizes the illusion is unreal, though he may still have instinctive reactions to it or choose to act as though it is still real to fool others.
Summon: This component creates or summons objects or creatures. Conjured objects cannot have any moving parts unless they are masterwork, and more complex items (like a lock) requires the arithmetician to have the skill to craft such an item and make an appropriate Craft check. The arithmetician can be either conjuring creatures from other planes, using raw magic or a suitable substrate to form them. Conjured creatures, usually called “minions” are under his control and will do as he commands without question; the arithmetician can modify the minions’ nature and abilities by using minion templates. It is easier to conjure a minion if the arithmetician has a “substrate” for that minion — appropriate material to create a minion of that type. For example, if the arithmetician wants to create an earth elemental, he could use the sands of the beach he stands on, or instead pull from the ocean to form a water elemental. Minions summoned using substrates are made out of said substrate, and any damage they sustain is also dealt to the substrate. 
Apocryphal: Effects that may or may not be allowed by a DM, do not expect to use these. They are listed as guidelines if the DM wishes to allow them.
Component Cost Reading Guide:
If a number has nothing else listed with it, that is its cost, you may take it only once.
If a number has a + in front of it, it can be taken multiple times by adding the listed value each time it is taken. 
If a number has a – in front of it, it reduces the component cost of the spell. It only affects the Required Component cost calculation if it is listed in a Required Component, and only affects the Effect Components cost calculation if it is listed in an Effect Component. You may take it only once, and any components that would conflict – such as the time it takes to cast a spell – cannot be taken in tandem.
If a number has a * behind it, it is a cumulative component cost, each increment costs the listed value plus the cost of all lesser values leading up to that value. For example, in Enhance, a +1 Will save bonus costs 1 component, a +2 save bonus costs 3 (1+2), +3 costs a total of 6 (1+2+3), +4 costs 10 (1+2+3+4) and so on.
Note: The points below are supposed to be used as is, and are balanced around normal play to make for easy spell building that should remain reasonable. In saying that, they are still guidelines, and if certain components or component combinations are found to be excessively strong or weak – especially when compared to what other spellcasters have available to them at your table – the arithmetician player and DM should work together to find more balanced costs for their spells. Certain combinations can have their spell level increased or decreased outside of what its component cost would recommend, or just not possible at all if they are found to be problematic.

Minion Templates: Templates are quick and easy ways to customize minions. A minion template is just a few quick adjustments to a minion’s statistics, giving the effect and feel of the appropriate minion without a ton of work.
• Advanced Template: +4 to all ability scores.
• Air Elemental Template: Immune to poison and wind. Attack deals +1d6 wind damage. Darkvision 60ft. +20 bonus to speed. Fly at its (modified) ground speed (perfect maneuverability). Weak to Ice. An air elemental typically looks like a tornado.
• Demon Template: Immune to poison. Earth resistance 10, ice resistance 10, fire resistance 10, lightning resistance 10. +4 bonus on damage rolls. +4 bonus on saves against spells and supernatural abilities. Darkvision 60ft. Weak to Holy.
• Earth Elemental Template: Immune to poison and earth. +5 natural armor bonus to AC. Improved Bull Rush. Darkvision 60ft. –10 penalty to speed. Weak to Wind. An earth elemental typically looks as if it is made of earth and stone; when still, an earth elemental looks like a statue.
• Fire Elemental Template: Immune to poison and fire. Attack deals +1d6 fire damage. Attacking it with natural weapons or unarmed attacks deals 1d6 fire damage to the attacker. Darkvision 60ft. +10 bonus to speed. Weak to Water. A fire elemental looks like an animate flame or a “special effect” of a creature made of fire; it can stand perfectly camouflaged within fires of its size or larger.
• Harmless Template: The minion is unable to directly cause harm — it cannot attack, use weapons, drop rocks on people from a rooftop and so on, but it could push a button that detonates a bomb. If attacked, a harmless minion does not retaliate (which makes it a good decoy for unintelligent enemies, as it lets its opponent chew on it until it expires).
• Holy Elemental Template: Immune to Holy. In areas of light, holy elementals become translucent. They gain a +6 to hit rolls and a dodge bonus to their AC while in bright light, reduced to a +3 while in normal light. In shadowy illumination, a holy elemental loses this translucence, having a faint glow that produces Dim Light out to 60ft. Weak to Shadow. Holy elementals look to have a radiant glow to them, almost as though they were made of light. 
• Ice Elemental Template: Immune to poison and ice. +5 natural armor bonus to AC. Improved Bull Rush. Darkvision 60ft. –10 penalty to speed. Weak to Fire. An ice elemental typically looks as if it is made of ice and snow; when still, an ice elemental looks like a snowman.
• Lightning Elemental Template: Immune to poison and lightning. Attack deals +1d6 lightning damage. Darkvision 60ft. +20 bonus to speed. Weak to Earth. Fly at its (modified) ground speed (perfect maneuverability). A lightning elemental typically looks like an animated jagged bolt of lightning.
• Shadow Elemental Template: Immune to Shadow. Attack deals +1d6 shadow damage. In any condition of illumination other than bright light, a shadow elemental disappears into the shadows, giving it concealment (20% miss chance). A shadow elemental can suspend or resume this ability as a free action. Darkvision within line of sight. Weak to Holy. A shadow elemental looks like an animate shadow, almost like an optical illusion as its two dimensional darkness takes a 3d shape.
• Skeleton Template: Immune to mental attacks (including charm and compulsion effects), absorbs shadow, poison, Con damage, and stunning. Damage reduction 5/bludgeoning. Darkvision 60ft. Weak to Holy. When lying still, a skeleton looks like any other (dead) skeleton.
• Water Elemental Template: Immune to poison and water. +5 natural armor bonus to AC. Darkvision 60ft. Swim speed equal to its ground speed +20. Can breathe underwater. Weak to Lightning. A water elemental looks like a free-standing wave, camouflaging perfectly into water.
• Zombie Template: Immune to mental attacks (including charm and compulsion effects), poison, absorbs shadow, Con damage, and stunning. +2 hit points per hit die. Damage reduction 5/slashing. Darkvision 60ft. Weak to Holy. All movement speeds are halved. When lying still, a zombie looks like any other dead body in the same state of decomposition.

Numerical Talents
Alongside his mathematical endeavors, an arithmetician will learn numerous talents that assist him in manipulating spells and other forms of magic. At 2nd level and every two levels thereafter, an arithmetician gains one numerical talent. An arithmetician cannot select an individual talent more than once. Talents marked with an asterisk (*) add effects to an arithmetician’s spellcasting ability. Only one of these talents can be applied to an individual spell and the decision must be made before the spell is cast.
Table: Numerical Talents
Numerical Talent
Prerequisites
Benefits
Additional Monster (Su)
— 
The arithmetician summons a monster(s) with a spell he summons one additional monster. This talent stacks with Superior Summoning if the spell is being used to summon 1d3 or 1d4+1 number of monsters. When using this talent on a spell, increase the MP cost by ½ of the spell level, this does not increase the spell level. 
Ambuscading Spell (Su)
— 
During a surprise round, the arithmetician’s opponents that have not yet acted take a –2 penalty on saving throws against spells he casts. Creatures that have already acted take a –1 penalty during the surprise round.
Arcane Builder (Ex)
—
The arithmetician has an exceptional understanding of the theory behind creating magical items. He can select one type of magic item (potions, wondrous items, and so on); he creates items of this type 25% faster than normal, and gains a +4 bonus on Spellcraft checks to craft items of this type. He may select this talent multiple times; its effects do not stack. Each time he selects this talent, it applies to a different type of magic item
Attract Disciple 
4th

Cancel Out (Su) 
8th
When you or an ally within 30 feet takes damage, you may use an immediate action to nullify certain values in the damage roll. An arithmetician chooses one of his known numbers, any die in that damage roll that shows the chosen number is treated as having rolled a 0 instead and does not contribute to the damage total.
You may use this ability once per creature protected per day.
Chaos Theory (Ex)
12th
Once per encounter, as an immediate action, the arithmetician can push his mathematical prowess to its limits, practically predicting the future via deterministic equations. Choose one creature the arithmetician can see, if that creature makes an attack roll, skill check, ability check, or saving throw before the start of your next turn. You may choose to add or subtract half your intelligence bonus on that roll. At 18th level, the modifier increases to your intelligence bonus.
Cognitive Thesis (Su) 
—
The arithmetician can condense and transmit highly complex information directly into the minds of others.
As a standard action, he may telepathically impart a complete understanding of an abstract or complex concept—such as an advanced mathematical theorem, intricate philosophical argument, or obscure historical context—to a number of willing creatures equal to his Intelligence modifier.
Targets must be within 60 feet. Upon receiving the information, the recipients comprehend it with perfect clarity and no ambiguity, regardless of their Intelligence score or prior knowledge. This does not grant skill ranks or abilities but allows perfect theoretical understanding.
Concentrate (Ex)
—
The arithmetician can reroll any concentration check he has just made with a +4 bonus. He must use this ability after the roll is made, but before the roll’s outcome is determined. The arithmetician must take the second roll, even if it is worse. The arithmetician can use this ability once per day.
Contingency Plan (Ex)
—
Once per encounter, if the arithmetician fails an attack roll, a skill check, or the use of a talent that requires an opposed check, he can move up to his movement speed as an immediate action.
Cup of Mercy (Su)
8th
Whenever an arithmetician casts a spell that deals damage, if it would reduce a creature’s hit points below 0, he can choose to let the damage reduce the creature to -1 HP and leave it stable. If he does so, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to the left over damage it was spared from.
Domain Exception (Su)
10th
Whenever a creature attempts to use a teleportation effect or summon a creature within 30 feet of the arithmetician, he may attempt to block the effect. Make an opposed caster level check (1d20 + caster level) as an immediate action. If the check succeeds, the spell or effect fails and is wasted; otherwise, it is unaffected. He can use this ability once per day plus one additional time for every five arithmetician levels he possesses beyond 10th.
Empower Disciple
Attract Disciple
Your minion now has Lil’ Witch levels equal to your class level, and gains an additional MP per level.
Familiar (Ex)
Caster Level 2nd. Must be chosen at 2nd level.
The arithmetician who selects this talent gains the Familiar feat.
Golden Ratio (Ex)
— 
Use your Intelligence bonus instead of your Charisma bonus for any roll relating to your appearance (such as disguise, seduction, making a good first impression).
Immortality (Ex)
20th
The arithmetician discovers a cure for aging, and from this point forward, he takes no penalty to his physical ability scores from advanced age and cannot die from old age. If he is already taking such penalties, they are removed at this time.
In Desperate Need of Coffee (Ex) 
—
The arithmetician treats non-lethal damage as lethal damage when determining if he can activate Limit Breaks, becoming fatigued after using a Limit Break in this manner.
Instruction Manual (Su)
—
The arithmetician gains the supernatural ability to speak with and understand any intelligent construct, even if they share no languages in common. Additionally, by observing a mindless construct for 3 rounds, the arithmetician can determine the nature of its instructions or programming, learning how the construct will respond to stimuli, like being attacked or approached. 
Knowledge is Power (Ex)
—
The arithmetician’s understanding of physical forces gives him power over them. He adds his Intelligence modifier on combat maneuver checks and to his CMD. He also adds his Intelligence modifier on Strength checks to break or lift objects.
Lies, Damned Lies, & Statistics (Ex) 
Above Average Magical Theorem:
The arithmetician may now take 11 on bluff checks. When telling a lie involving any form of math, he may treat it as the truth for any abilities or magic that detects or affects the truthfulness of the statement. (Eq, he can now say 1+1=3 under the effects of a zone of truth. This does not mean others will believe such obvious lies, and a check may still be required to convince them.)
Mage Training
—
The arithmetician may select an item creation or metamagic feat. The arithmetician must still meet all prerequisites for a bonus feat, including caster level minimums. This talent may be taken more than once. Each time, a different feat must be selected.
Magic Aid (Su)
—
As a standard action, the arithmetician can spend MP up to his maximum spell level to grant additional magic energy to an allied spellcaster within close range (25 feet + 5 feet/2 levels). If that ally casts a spell of an equal or lower MP cost before the beginning of his next turn, all level-dependent calculations and caster level checks the spell requires are made as if the ally’s caster level were 2 higher. If MP spent is at least twice the MP cost of the spell his ally casts, his ally’s caster level is treated as 4 higher instead. If his ally is able to cast more than one spell before the beginning of his next turn, only the first spell cast gains this bonus.
Mathematical Paradox (Su): 
—
As a standard action, you force one creature within 60 feet of you to attempt to conceptualize a paradox or logical contradiction so baffling that it overloads their mind. That creature must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + ½ your character level + your Intelligence modifier) or be stunned for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect. This effect ignores construct immunities and they automatically fail their saving throw. You may use this ability a number of times per day equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).
Reserve Training
—
The arithmetician may select a Reserve feat as a bonus feat. The arithmetician must still meet all prerequisites for this bonus feat
Restless Scholar (Su)
6th
The arithmetician can go without eating or drinking for a number of days equal to his Intelligence modifier before he must make Constitution checks to avoid nonlethal damage. Additionally, he can spend 8 hours studying his spells instead of sleeping. This confers the same benefit as an 8 hour rest, but he is awake the entire time.
Rod Mastery (Su)
—
Whenever the arithmetician uses a rod, he calculates the DC for any spell it contains using his Intelligence modifier (minimum 0) instead of the minimum modifier needed to cast a spell of that level.
Rod Wielder (Su)
—
The arithmetician adds his Intelligence bonus (minimum 0) on caster level checks made to overcome spell resistance when using a spell contained within a rod.
Round Reality (Su) 
12th
You gain the ability to manipulate the numerical structure of reality, changing figures to the nearest value. As an immediate action, you may choose any single numerical value within range (60 feet) and round it up or down to the first significant figure, allowing you to alter a numerical value—such as a measurement, or the price of an item— (e.g., increasing a 16-foot jump distance to 20 feet, or reducing a 450 gp potion’s price to 400 gp). You must choose to round either up or down, and the number must remain positive after rounding. 
This ability cannot create or destroy matter, and cannot be used to produce impossible, paradoxical, or non-numeric effects. If the result of the rounding would negatively affect a creature (e.g., reducing the gold they receive, increasing their internal body temperature, or modifying an effect they control), the target gets a save of an appropriate type as determined by the DM (e.g., If one is warping the value of a potion that costs 450 gp to make it 400, a will save for the financial damage, or a fortitude save if you are targeting someones internal body temperature)
You may use this ability three times per day.
Sacrificial Numbers (Su)
12th
If the arithmetician’s hit points would fall below 0, he may sacrifice one of his summoned creatures as an immediate action. If he does so, the summoned creature instantly dies, and the arithmetician is reduced to 0 hit points instead. He may do this once per day.
Speed Calculus (Ex) 
—
As a standard action, once per day, the arithmetician can replace one of his memorized spells with a new one. The new spell gains the benefits of the arithmeticians discount if it is replacing one that was already discounted.
Speed of Thought (Ex) 
—
The arithmetician can no longer be surprised, and always act during a surprise round. In addition, the arithmetician may dismiss any spell he has cast as a free action.
Spell Lore (Ex)
—
The arithmetician adds his level to all Spellcraft checks made to identify a spell being cast. (This is most often useful when attempting to counterspell.)
Spell Sage (Ex)

When the arithmetician attempts a Use Magic Device check to cast a spell from a materia, he gains a +4 competence bonus to the check.
Surecast (Su)
Combat Casting feat
The arithmetician exercises caution when in danger, casting his spells with more care. While in a threatened square, he may choose to spend a full-round action to cast a spell, with a casting time of standard action or less. Doing so allows him to cast the spell without needing to cast defensively.
Think on It (Ex)
— 
One per day, the arithmetician can re-attempt any previously failed Knowledge check. On this attempt, he adds a +5 competence bonus on the check. At 10th level, this bonus increases to +10.
Tranquil Mind (Ex) 
— 
The arithmetician gets a bonus on all concentration checks equal to your constitution modifier. 
Wand Mastery (Su)
—
Whenever the arithmetician uses a wand, he calculates the DC for any spell it contains using his Intelligence modifier, instead of the minimum modifier needed to cast a spell of that level.
Metamagic Talents
Talents marked with an asterisk (*) add effects to a black mage’s spellcasting ability. Only one of these talents can be applied to an individual spell and the decision must be made before the spell is cast.
Empowered Magic (Su)
—
The arithmetician can cast one spell per day as if it were modified by the Empower Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.

—
The arithmetician can cast two spells per day as if they were modified by the Extend Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.

The arithmetician can cast one spell per day as if it were modified by the Quicken Spell feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.
Reach Magic (Su)
—
The arithmetician can cast two spells per day as if they were modified by the Reach Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.
Selective Magic (Su)
—
The arithmetician can cast two spells per day as if they were modified by the Selective Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.
Silent Magic (Su)
—
The arithmetician can cast two spells per day as if they were modified by the Silent Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.

—
The arithmetician can cast two spells per day as if they were modified by the Still Spell metamagic feat. This does not increase the MP cost or the level of the spell.
Spellcasting ability*
Talents marked with an asterisk (*) add effects to an arithmetician’s spellcasting ability. Only one of these talents can be applied to an individual spell and the decision must be made before the spell is cast.
Creative Destruction (Su)*
—
The arithmetician has learned how to use destructive energy to empower himself. When he casts a spell with flexible spellcasting that deals damage, he gains a number of temporary hit points equal to the total number of dice used to determine the damage caused by the spell. Temporary hit points gained from this talent disappear after 1 hour.
Defensive Feedback (Su)*
—
Rather than dissipate damaging energy, the arithmetician can redirect some of it back to its source. When an enhancing spell the arithmetician casts prevents damage (with damage reduction or energy resistance), if the attacking creature is within 30 feet of the protected creature, the foe takes 1d6 points of damage (of the same damage type that was prevented) for every 10 points of damage prevented.

—

—
