limitBreaks.name: Defensive Numbers
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break allows the arithmetician to divide damage coming at him and his party. The arithmetician and all allies within a 30-ft.-radius of the arithmetician takes half damage from any source for a duration of 1 round + 1 round per four arithmetician levels after 1st. This limit break requires only a swift action.

limitBreaks.name: Null Zero Effect
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break allows the arithmetician to cast spells without any spell exhaustion. For a duration of 1 round + 1 round per four arithmetician levels after 1st, any spell you cast doesn’t incur any spell exhaustion. This limit break requires only a swift action.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: Vampires are proficient with all simple and martial weapons. They are also proficient with light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields). A vampire gains a slam attack. Damage for the slam depends on the vampire’s size (1d4 for small, 1d6 for medium, and 1d8 for large). His slam also causes energy drain (see below). His natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

features.name: Undead Traits
features.text:
A vampire possesses the following traits.
• The vampire has no Constitution score. He uses his Charisma score in place of his Constitution score when calculating hit points, Fortitude saves, and any special ability that relies on Constitution (such as when calculating a breath weapon’s DC).
• The vampire is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, morale effects, patterns, and phantasms).
• The vampire is not subject to nonlethal damage, ability drain, or energy drain. He is immune to damage to his physical ability scores (Constitution, Dexterity, and Strength), as well as to exhaustion and fatigue effects.
• The vampire absorbs all shadow damage, healing from any shadow damage that would have been taken.
• The vampire is weak against holy damage, taking half again holy damage taken.
• The vampire is considered undead for healing spells and effects.
• The vampire gains Darkvision 60 feet. If he already has Darkvision, it increases by 30 feet instead.
• The vampire is immune to death effects, disease, paralysis, poison, sleep effects, and stunning.
• The vampire is not affected by raise and reincarnate spells or abilities. Arise, arisega, and full-life can affect undead creatures. These spells turn undead creatures back into the living creatures they were before becoming undead. If this happens to a vampire, he no longer has access to vampire class features and must progress into another class. If she is turned back into a vampire, then she can progress as a vampire normally.

features.name: Blood Pool
features.text:
At 1st level, a vampire has a blood pool in which he can use to heal his wounds or use one of his disciplines. The vampire’s maximum blood is equal to 3 + his vampire level + his Charisma modifier. The vampire begins play with half of his maximum blood pool.
By spending 1 blood point as a swift action, the vampire can do one of the following:
• Increase his speed by 10 feet for 1 round, or
• Heal himself for 5 points of damage (a vampire can spend multiple blood points to heal more, but not more than half her vampire level, minimum 1), or
• Increase one saving throw by +1 for 1 round.
As long as the vampire has at least 1 blood point in his blood pool, he is calm. Once he runs out of blood points, he frenzies. When this happens, the vampire gets the Berserk status effect and must feed on his closest enemy target (or non-enemy target if none are around) until he gains 1 blood point. He must then make a Will save (DC 20 – the number of blood points he has in his blood pool) to stop frenzying. The vampire can make a (DC 25) Will save to stop the frenzy from ever happening. But he must make this same Will save for each round that he is out of blood points.

features.name: Shadowless
features.text: At 1st level, a vampire casts no shadows and shows no reflection in a mirror.

features.name: Clans
features.text:
At 1st level, a vampire usually belongs to a clan of vampires. Choose one of the thirteen.
• Animal Clan: Often closer to beasts than other vampires.
• Clan Disciplines: Animalism, Fortitude, and Protean
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Cha.
• Assassin Clan: The clan of enforcers.
• Clan Disciplines: Celerity, Obfuscate, and Blood Sorcery
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Cha.
• Special: The Assamite vampire has toxic blood. Whenever any creature adjacent to this vampire strikes him with a manufacture weapon, natural attack, or unarmed strike, they take 1d6 points of earth damage each time.
• Beauty Clan: Known for their seductive nature. Supernaturally graceful and charming, these vamlpires are always looking for the next thrill, leaving a detritus of discarded lovers and victims in their wake.
• Clan Disciplines: Auspex, Celerity, and Presence
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Cha
• Brute Clan: The clan of troublemakers who seek to fight.
• Clan Disciplines: Celerity, Potence, and Presence
• Clan Stats: +2 Str, +2 Cha.
• Special: Starting combat in front of this vampire causes them to frenzy unless they make a Will save (DC 20 – the number of blood points in his blood pool).
• Clanless: These are vampires without a clan.
• Clan Disciplines: Pick 3 different disciplines, these become his standard disciplines.
• Clan Stats: Pick two different ability scores, 1 physical (besides Con) and 1 mental.
• Special: When dealing with other clans, this vampire suffers a -2 penalty on all Charisma checks as the clanless are all looked down upon.
• Crazy Clan: Derided as Lunatics by other vampires.
• Clan Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, and Obfuscate
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Wis.
• Special: These vampires gain one additional drawback.
• Cursed Clan: This clan wear their curse on the outside.
• Clan Disciplines: Animalism, Obfuscate, and Potence
• Clan Stats: -2 Dex, +2 Int, +2 Wis, +2 Cha.
• Special: This vampire suffers a -4 penalty on all Charisma skills except Animal Handling.
• Illusion Clan: Masters of misdirection clan.
• Clan Disciplines: Animalism, Obfuscate, and Presence
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Cha.
• Special: This vampire’s BAB reduces to half and he gains the MP pool and spells of an illusionist equal to his vampire level. He loses proficiency with weapons and armor, only gaining proficiency with power rods and power staves.
• Leader Clan: Often called the clan of leadership, these vampires rule supreme among other vampire clans.
• Clan Disciplines: Dominate, Fortitude, and Presence
• Clan Stats: +2 Wis, +2 Cha.
• Shadow Clan: A sneaky clan develop in the shadows.
• Clan Disciplines: Dominate, Potence, and Umbra
• Clan Stats: +2 Str, +2 Int.
• Sorcerer Clan: The clan of arcane vampires.
• Clan Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, and Blood Sorcery
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Int.
• Special: A vampire’s BAB reduces to half and he gains the MP pool and spells of a black mage equal to his vampire level. He loses proficiency with weapons and armor, only gaining proficiency with power rods and power staves.
• The Possessed Clan: To these vampires, possessions are all they care about.
• Clan Disciplines: Animalism, Dominate, and Protean
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Int.
• Time Clan: These vampires deal all about chronomancy.
• Clan Disciplines: Celerity, Dominate, and Presence
• Clan Stats: +2 Dex, +2 Int.
• Special: This vampire’s BAB reduces to half and he gains the MP pool and spells of a time mage equal to his vampire level. He loses proficiency with weapons and armor, only gaining proficiency with power rods and power staves.

features.name: Disciplines
features.text:
Starting at 1st level a vampire gains the first discipline ability in each of his starting clan disciplines. At 3rd level and every two vampire levels thereafter he advances one of his disciplines, gaining the next ability.
• Animalism: Utilized by those who desire a close and supernatural bond with the animal world as well as a vampire’s own Beast. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Animalism, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus to his Handle Animal checks.
• Bond Famulus (Ex): A vampire with this discipline gains a service of an animal companion as a beastmaster of his vampire level.
• Feral Whispers (Ex): A vampire is able to speak with animals like a beastmaster.
• Quell the Beast (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire is able to calm another vampire’s frensy or a non-vampire to sleep. A vampire affected by this can’t rage or frenzy without a save. A non-vampire affected by this needs to make a Will save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or fall asleep for 1 round per level.
• Subsume the Spirit (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use the spell, Dominate Monster, but only affect animals.
• Animal Dominion (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use the spell, Dominate Monster, but only affect all animals of same type in a 50-feet-radius.
• Auspex: Enables vampires to hone their senses both physical and psychic in order to bolster his awareness, perceptions, or even see visions of the future. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Auspex, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus to his Perception checks.
• Heightened Senses (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire adds 30 feet of darkvision, gains low-light vision, and gains +5 insight bonus of Perception checks for a duration of 1 minute per level.
• Unerring Pursuit (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire gains a +5 insight bonus on Survival checks to track a creature for a duration of 1 hour per level.
• Vermin Vision (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can see the vision from any animal within 50 feet.
• Clairaudience/Clairvoyance (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire is able use Clairaudience/Clairvoyance, as per the spell.
• Telepathy (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire gains telepathy out to 100 ft. and can communicate with any creature, regardless of intelligence, so long as they have an Intelligence of 1 or higher. The range of his telepathy increases by 10 ft. every vampire level thereafter. If the vampire has a form of telepathy, this ability adds to his range.
• Blood Sorcery: A type of blood magic that allows the practitioners to manipulate the blood, mortal or vampiric. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Blood Sorcery, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus to his Spellcraft checks.
• Corrosive Vitae (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause another creature’s blood to become acidic. A creature within 30 feet must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or suffer 1d6 points of Constitution damage.
• Blood’s Curse (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause another creature’s blood to become cursed. A creature within 30 feet must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or suffer the Curse and Disease status effect and take 1d2 points of Constitution damage per round for a duration of 1 round per vampire level.
• Scorpion’s Touch (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause his own blood to have a paralyzing poison effect. For a duration of 1 round per level, whenever the vampire would be struck by a manufacture weapon, natural weapon or unarmed strike, the attacker must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or be paralyzed for 1 round.
• Theft of Vitae (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can steal the blood of his victims. A creature within 30 feet must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or take 1d4+1 points of Condition drain. The vampire gains blood points equal to the Constitution drain.
• Reclamation of Vitae (Su): At a cost of 1 or more blood points, a vampire can spend some blood boosting his combat prowess. For a duration of 1 round per vampire levels, the vampire is hasted and for each blood point spent, the vampire gains 5 temporary hit points and a +2 competence bonus to his Strength and Charisma.
• Celerity: Powers up the movement of the vampire, enabling him to have unnatural quickness in his movement and supernatural reflexes. Passive bonus: For each tier taken in Celerity, it boosts the vampire’s movement speed by 5 feet.
• Rapid Reflexes: A vampire gains Combat Reflexes as a bonus feat.
• Fleetness (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire becomes hasted for a duration of 1 round per vampire level.
• A Thousand Cuts (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use flurry of blows like a monk, but usable with any weapons and stacking with haste, for 1 round.
• Draught of Elegance (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can haste himself and all other allies within 30 feet for 1 round per vampire level.
• Lightning Strike (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause lightning to strike with his melee strikes. For a duration of 1 round per vampire level, a vampire’s melee attacks deal an extra +2d6 points of lightning damage.
• Dominate: Allows the vampire to use mind control through eye contact and spoken word as well as manipulate memories of his victims. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Dominate, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus to his Diplomacy checks.
• Compel (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use command, as per the spell.
• Mesmerize (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use hypnotism, as per the spell.
• Chain of Command (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use suggestion, as per the spell.
• Tabula Rasa (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause another creature to erase the victim’s memory to the point they don’t know who they are. A creature within 30 feet must make a Will save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or forget their memory for a duration of 1 round per vampire level.
• Mass Manipulation (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use mass suggestion, as per the spell.
• Fortitude: Strengthens the vampire’s physical and mental resistance. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Fortitude, it boosts a vampire’s resistance to damage. A vampire gains DR 1/- and 2 elemental resistance (all).
• Resilience (Ex): A vampire gains a number of bonus hit points equal to his vampire level.
• Invigorating Vitae (Su): Every time a vampire would heal by spending blood points, he heals additional health equal to his Charisma modifier.
• Fortify the Inner Facade (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, as a swift action, a vampire can end an enfeebling effect on him.
• Draught of Endurance (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, as a swift action, a vampire can end 1 enfeebling effect on him and all allies within 30 feet.
• Flesh of Marble (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use stoneskin, as per the spell.
• Obfuscate: The art of not being seen even in crowds either through being wholly unseen or by blending in. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Obfuscate, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus to his Stealth checks.
• Silence of Death (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire radiates silence up to 20 feet as if affected by a silent object
• Unseen Passage (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use disappear, as per the spell.
• Mask of a Thousand Faces (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use disguise self, as per the spell.
• Vanish (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use vanish, as per the spell.
• Cloak the Gathering (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can use vanishga, as per the spell.
• Potence: Strengthens the vampire’s physical prowess. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Potence, it boosts a vampire’s Strength score by +1.
• Soaring Leap (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire gains the use of the jump class feature of dragoons, for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Prowess (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire’s BAB increases to equal his vampire level for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Spark of Rage (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can rage like a berserker of his vampire level.
• Draught of Might (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire and his allies within 30 feet can rage like a berserker of his vampire level.
• Earth Shock (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can cause a shockwave of earth to ripple through his enemies. All enemies in a 30-ft.-cone must make a Reflex save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or take 1d6 points of earth/physical damage per vampire level, half damage on a successful save.
• Presence: Enables the vampire to use subtle manipulation, control, and swaying of emotions to guide others towards a goal. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Presence, it boosts a vampire’s Charisma score by +1.
• Awe (Ex): For every tier spent in Presence, it grants the vampire a +2 competence bonus on Diplomacy and Intimidate skill checks.
• Eyes of the Serpent (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can immobilize a creature within 30 feet that he can see. Target creature must make a Will save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or become immobilized for 1 round per vampire level.
• Dread Gaze (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can instill fear, as per spell.
• Summon (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can summon to appear before him as fast as possible. Target creature must have met the vampire in person and must be within 1 mile per vampire level. A creature summoned must make a Will save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or must make all haste to where the vampire is currently standing, whether or not he is still there by the time the summoned creature arrives.
• Majesty (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can invoke majesty. All enemies within a 50-foot radius that can see the vampire must make a Will save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or become disabled for 1 round per vampire level.
• Protean: Grants the ability to change one’s shape, grow claws, meld into the earth, or become a swarm. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Protean, it boosts a vampire’s saving throws by +1.
• Eyes of the Beast (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can see in darkness, magical or otherwise, for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Feral Weapons (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire grows claws that deal 1d4 points of slashing damage (1d3 if small, 1d6 if large) and his teeth sharpens, giving him a bite attack that deals 1d6 points of damage (1d4 if small, 1d8 if large), for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Earth Meld (Ex): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire gains burrow 20 feet and can pass through stone, dirt, or almost any other sort of earth except metal as easily as a fish swims through water. If protected against fire damage, it can even glide through lava. His burrowing leaves behind no tunnel or hole, nor does it create any ripple or other sign of his presence for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Metamorphosis (Sp): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can change his shape into a beast, as beast shape III or IV, per the spell.
• Swarm (Su): At a cost of 1 blood point, a vampire can transform into a swarm of vermin. He doesn’t leave his gear behind when he uses this ability, and he can revert to his mundane form normally for a duration of 1 minute per vampire level.
• Umbra: The signature power of the Shadow Clan. The Umbra grants the vampire power over darkness itself. Some believe it to be merely shadows, while others feel the power gives control over the stuff of the vampire’s soul, coaxing it tangibility outward. Passive Bonus: For each tier taken in Umbra, the target takes an additional 1 point of shadow damage from all Umbra discipline abilities affecting or directed at the target(s).
• Shadow Play (Su) By spending 1 blood point, the vampire gains limited control over shadows and other ambient darkness. He may take an existing shadow, including those shed by other creatures, and stretch to replicate the darkness spell within that area. The caster level is equal to his vampire level. The vampire can see in this darkness perfectly and with no penalty.
• Shroud of Night (Su) At the cost of 1 blood point, the vampire with this discipline can create a cloud of inky black darkness that clings to targets up to 25 feet away + additional 5 feet per two vampire levels away in a 20-ft.-radius. Targets hit by this ability must make a Reflex save (DC 10 + half of the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or be under the effects of entangle status effect. Entangled creatures can attempt a Strength check or Escape Artist skill check, (DC 10 + half of the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier). If the target(s) turn ends within the shroud, they take 1d6 shadow damage per three vampire levels attained.
• Arms of the Abyss (Su) By spending 1 blood pool point, the vampire may use surrounding shadows to attack the chosen targets. These tendrils of shadow function as the Dark spell with a caster level equal to the vampire’s level. Every other level after first, the vampire may call on an additional shadow tendril to attack the same, or a separate target, to a maximum of 10 tendrils at 20th level. The DC for the Obscure status effect is (DC 10 + half of the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier).
• Black Metamorphosis (Su) At the cost of 1 blood point, as a move action, and lasts a number of rounds equal to the vampire’s Charisma Modifier, he becomes a hybrid of matter and shadow. His attacks instead deal shadow damage in place of its normal damage type. Also, while under the effects of Black Metamorphosis, he benefits from the Umbral Spikes spell with a caster level equal to his vampire level. At 11th level, this becomes Umbral Spikes ll, and at 15th level, Umbral Spikes lll.
• Tenebrous Form (Su) By spending 1 blood point, as a free action, the vampire takes on a form of pure darkness. While under this effect, all damage is reduced by half (with the exception of holy and fire). The vampire may also slither through cracks and tight spaces while under this effect. The vampire’s melee attacks deal no damage while in this form. In addition, all shadow damage dealt from class abilities is maximized. This form lasts for 1 round per vampire level and be canceled as a free action at any time.

features.name: Blood Drain
features.text:
Starting at 1st level, a vampire can attempt to bite a victim with his growing fangs and suck blood. If the vampire makes a successful grapple check and pins the foe, it sucks blood, dealing 1 point of Constitution damage each round that the pin is maintained. With each such successful attack, the vampire gains 1 blood point and 1 temporary hit point (up to a maximum number of temporary hit points equal to his full normal hit points).
When the vampire reaches 2nd level, his fangs are fully developed, though he has not yet perfected his technique for drawing blood. At this point, his blood drain attack deals 1 point of Constitution drain and gains back 1 blood point.
At 4th level, the vampire has mastered the art of drawing blood from a victim. His blood drain attack deals 1d4 points of Constitution drain (gaining blood points equal to the Constitution drain), and he gains 5 temporary hit points with each successful blood drain.

features.name: Resistances
features.text: At 1st level, the vampire gains ice resistance 5 and lightning resistance 5. When he reaches 5th level, each of these resistances increases to 10.

features.name: Spider Climb
features.text: At 2nd level, a vampire can climb sheer surfaces as though under the effects of a wall climb spell.

features.name: Vampire Stats
features.text:
At 2nd level, a vampire gains a +2 bonus to his Strength scores.
At 6th level, he gains a +2 bonus to his Dexterity and Charisma scores.
At 10th level, he gains a +2 bonus to his Strength, Intelligence, and Wisdom scores.
At 14th level, he gains a +2 bonus to his Strength scores.
At 18th level, he gains a +2 bonus to his Dexterity and Charisma scores.

features.name: Coffin Sanctuary
features.text:
Upon reaching 3rd level, a vampire chooses a coffin or similar small enclosed space as his primary resting place. Thereafter, if he is brought to -1 to -9 hit points (if living) or to 0 or fewer hit points (if undead) while outside the coffin, he is forced to assume gaseous form (see below) immediately and flee for his coffin so that he may heal. If the vampire cannot use his vampiric ability to assume gaseous form (for example, if he has expended all his daily uses of that ability), he cannot enter gaseous form under these circumstances and dies immediately.
Any damage dealt to the vampire after he is forced into gaseous form has no effect. If the duration of his gaseous form ability expires before he reaches his coffin, or more than 2 hours pass after he is forced into gaseous form in this way, the vampire must assume his normal form at his current location. In that case, he either begins to die (if he is a living vampire) or is destroyed (if he is an undead vampire). If he succeeds in reaching his coffin, he is helpless for 1 hour, after which he heals 1 hit point and the helplessness ends. A non-helpless vampire resting in his coffin has fast healing 1.
A 5th-level or higher non-helpless vampire resting in his coffin has fast healing 5.

features.name: Gaseous Form
features.text:
Starting at 3rd level, a vampire can assume gaseous form as the spell (caster level equal to his vampire level) once per day as a standard action. He can remain in gaseous form for up to 10 minutes. A gaseous vampire’s fly speed is 20 feet.
At 5th level, a vampire can assume gaseous form three times per day. At 7th level, he may become gaseous at will and remain in gaseous form indefinitely.

features.name: Change Shape
features.text: At 4th level, a vampire can use change shape to assume the form of a dire bat or wolf, as beast shape II spell.

features.name: Fast Healing
features.text:
Beginning at 4th level, a vampire heals 1 point of damage each round so long as he has at least 1 hit point, whether or not he is resting in his coffin. A living vampire reduced to fewer than 0 hp or an undead vampire reduced to 0 hit points is automatically forced into gaseous form (if he still has uses of that ability available) and must retreat to his coffin (see the Coffin Sanctuary, above).
At 9th level, a vampire’s fast healing increases to 5.

features.name: Sunlight & Water Vulnerability
features.text:
A 5th-level or higher vampire exposed to direct sunlight is disoriented. While in this condition, he can take only a single move action or attack action in a round, and 3 full rounds of such exposure destroy it utterly. Similarly, immersing a typical vampire in running water robs it of one-fifth of its hit points each round until it is destroyed at the end of the fifth round of immersion. (A vampire with a natural swim speed is not harmed by immersion in running water.)
At 11th level, a vampire’s flesh becomes even more vulnerable to sunlight and running water. Upon exposure to sunlight, he takes the above penalties and is destroyed utterly in the next round if he cannot escape. The vampire loses one-third of his hit points each round of immersion in water instead of one-fifth, and he is destroyed after at the end of the third round of exposure instead of the fifth round.

features.name: Children of the Night
features.text: At 5th level, once per day, a vampire can call forth 1d6+1 rat swarms, 1d4+1 bat swarms, or 2d6 wolves as a standard action. (If the base creature is not terrestrial, this power might summon other creatures of similar power.) These creatures arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve the vampire for up to 1 hour.

features.name: Natural Hide
features.text: At 6th and every two vampire levels thereafter, a vampire’s natural armor to AC increases by +1.

features.name: Energy Drain
features.text:
When the vampire reaches 7th level, any living creature hit by his slam attack (or any other natural weapon he might possess) gains one negative level. For each negative level so bestowed, the vampire gains 5 temporary hit points. This ability only triggers once per round, regardless of the number of attacks a vampire makes. If an attack that includes an energy drain scores a critical hit, it bestows twice the listed number of negative levels. These temporary hit points last for a maximum of 1 hour. Negative levels remain until 24 hours have passed or until they are removed with a spell, such as restora. If a negative level is not removed before 24 hours have passed, the affected creature must attempt a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the draining creature’s racial HD + draining creature’s Charisma modifier; the exact DC is given in the creature’s descriptive text). On a success, the negative level goes away with no harm to the creature. On a failure, the negative level becomes permanent. A separate saving throw is required for each negative level.
At 9th level, the vampire’s slam attack (or other natural attack) bestows 2 negative levels.

features.name: Create Spawn
features.text:
A humanoid or monstrous humanoid slain by a 7th-level or higher vampire’s energy drain attack rises as a vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. If the vampire instead drains the victim’s Constitution to 0 or lower, the victim returns as a spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD and as a vampire if it had 5 or more HD. In either case, the new vampire or spawn is under the command of the vampire that created it and remains so enslaved until its master’s destruction.
At any given time, a vampire may have enslaved spawn whose Hit Dice total no more than his own. Any spawn he creates that would exceed this limit can be created either as free-willed vampires or as vampire spawn, at the creator’s option. If he chooses the latter option, he must immediately free one or more spawn of his choice until the total Hit Dice of his existing enslaved spawn would allow the addition of the desired new one. Once freed, a vampire or vampire spawn cannot be enslaved again, except through magic such as control undead. An enslaved vampire may create and enslave spawn of its own, so a master vampire can control a large number of lesser vampires in this fashion.
At 8th level, the vampire may have enslaved spawn whose Hit Dice total no more than twice his own Hit Dice.
Vampire Spawn: A vampire can elect to create a vampire spawn instead of a full-fledged vampire when he uses his create spawn ability on a humanoid creature only. This decision must be made as a free action whenever a vampire slays an appropriate creature by using blood drain or energy drain. A vampire spawn’s statistics are identical to those of a wight, save for the following changes.
• It gains the blood drain and dominate vampire special attacks.
• It gains channel resistance +2, DR 5/silver, resist cold and energy 10, fast healing 2, and the vampire qualities listed above (gaseous form, shadowless, and spider climb).
• A vampire spawn gains all of the standard vampire weaknesses.
• A vampire spawn is CR 4.

features.name: Dominate
features.text:
At 8th level, a vampire gains the ability to crush another creature’s will just by looking into its eyes. This ability is similar to a gaze attack, except that the vampire must use a standard action, and those merely looking at him are not affected. Anyone the vampire targets must succeed on a Will save or fall instantly under his influence, as though via a dominate person/monster spell (caster level equal to his vampire level). The ability has a range of 10 feet and is usable once per day.
At 10th level, the vampire can use this ability three times per day at a range of 20 feet. At 12th level, his range increases to 30 feet. At 14th level, the vampire may use his dominate ability at will.

features.name: Fortification
features.text:
When the vampire reaches 13th level, his internal organs begin to cease functioning as they become unnecessary to his altered metabolism. This process makes him less vulnerable to critical hits, sneak attacks, and other attacks that target a creature’s vital spots. The vampire is treated as if he had the light fortification armor property active at all times. This ability gives him a 25% chance to turn a critical hit or sneak attack against him into a normal attack. If the vampire already has fortification from another source (such as a spell or magic item), use the better value.
At 15th level, this ability becomes moderate fortification (50% chance to turn a critical hit or sneak attack into a normal attack). At 17th level, this ability becomes heavy fortification (75% chance to turn a critical hit or sneak attack into a normal attack). At 19th level, this ability becomes full fortification (automatically turns a critical hit or sneak attack into a normal attack).

features.name: Masa Dominate
features.text: At 16th level, a vampire can use his dominate ability on all enemies within 30 feet.

features.name: Master Vampire
features.text: At 20th level, a vampire becomes a master vampire. He no longer takes damage in sunlight or running water. The DCs of all his vampire class features increase by 2.

limitBreaks.name: Blood Cloud
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break allows the vampire to drain the blood of his victims. Enemies within 30 feet of the vampire must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half the vampire’s level + his Charisma modifier) or they will 1d4 points of Constitution damage + an additional 1d4 per four vampire levels after 1st. The vampire gains a number of blood points equal to the Condition damage suffered. If the vampire has more blood points than his max when this Limit Break ends, he loses the extra. This Limit Break requires a standard action.

limitBreaks.name: Perfect Vampire
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break perfects the vampire’s vampirism. For a duration of 1 round + 1 round per four vampire levels after 1st, the vampire gains immunity to Holy damage and sunlight. In addition, he also gains a +2 competence bonus to his class feature DCs + an additional +1 DC per four vampire levels after 1st. Finally, his maximum blood pool doubles. If the vampire has more blood points than his max when this Limit Break ends, he loses the extra. This Limit Break requires a swift action.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The commonfolk is proficient with one simple weapon. He is not proficient with any other weapons, nor is he proficient with any type of armor or shield.

features.name: Allies of the Fields
features.text: Due to his efforts in the fields, farming crops for his fellows, the commonfolk is seen as an ally of any other commonfolk. Once per day, If he is within shouting distance of any other commonfolk he can shout for aid, having any commonfolk that are not hostile towards them to come running to assist him. Commonfolk can help in combat scenarios as well as using aid another for skill checks.

features.name: Camaraderie of Neighbours
features.text: At 5th level, the commonfolk is well known amongst his settlement, enough to the point he can call on even more aid either through a louder voice or by others spreading the word. Once per day, the commonfolk can attract the attention of 1 Influencer and 1 Lil’ witch when using his allies of the fields (this does not count as a use for that ability), though these NPCs only help with one activity.

features.name: All Together
features.text: At 10th level, the commonfolk can give out commands to his fellows and have them listen to them without question. Whenever the commonfolk flanks an opponent with another commonfolk, he gains a +4 bonus to attack rolls instead of the normal +2, and for every commonfolk after the first that is adjacent to the same enemy, he gains an additional +1 bonus (flanking and 2 adjacent would be +6 total). This bonus stacks with Outflank to being +6 when flanking.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The disciple of the land is proficient with one simple weapon (usually a pick axe, an axe, or a sickle, depending on his profession). He is not proficient with any other weapons, nor is he proficient with any type of armor or shield.

features.name: Gatherer Profession
features.text:
At 1st level, a disciple of the land must choose one of the three professions: Botanist, Fisher, Miner.
• A botanist receives the following items for free: A handaxe and a sickle.
• A fisher receives the following items for free: A fishhook, fishing tackle, fishing net, and a brass knife.
• A miner receives the following items for free: A pickaxe and light hammer.
A disciple of the land is proficient with all received weapons from his gatherer profession in addition to his starting weapon proficiency. In addition, a disciple of the land receives a +2 competence bonus on Profession checks.

features.name: Material Sight
features.text: At 5th level, a disciple of the land knows instinctively of where ore is located, the best wood/plants to harvest from, or even know where the best fishing spot. A disciple of the land gains a 60-ft. range of knowing these things.

features.name: Gathering Expertise
features.text:
At 10th level, a disciple of the land gains an expertise with his chosen profession. At 13th level and every three disciple of the land levels thereafter, he gets to choose another expertise.
• Bountiful Yield (Ex): This ability increases the number of items a disciple of the land gains by harvesting by 1 (only items from harvesting, does not work with the giving land ability). This can be selected more than once.
• Sharp Vision (Ex): This ability increases the disciple of the land’s material sight by 30 feet. This can be selected more than once.
• The Giving Land (Ex): This ability allows the disciple of the land to gain an elemental shard (of his choice) when harvesting. This can be only selected once.

features.name: Bounty of Nature
features.text: Once per day at 15th level, the disciple of the land can bless a meal of fishes, fruits, grains, or vegetables so that, when consumed prior to resting, it increases the amount of natural healing from which a creature benefits after an eight-hour rest. This blessing can affect a number of creatures equal to half his disciple of the land level plus his Wisdom modifier. Each affected creature regains 2 hit points per Hit Die and one additional point of ability damage to a single ability score of its choice after resting. At 20th level, each affected creature regains 3 hit points per Hit Die and one additional point of ability damage to every ability score that has been damaged after resting.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The influencer is proficient in the use of all simple and martial weapons and with all types of armor and shields.

features.name: Noble Tongue
features.text: The influencer is able to talk to most any folk within settlements, allowing him to easily gain information or have others see his way of things. At 1st level, the influencer gains a +1 bonus on Diplomacy checks, this increases by +1 every 5 levels thereafter.

features.name: Defense Teachings
features.text: At 3rd level, the influencer is able to pay for knightly services, teaching how to better protect himself about the cities as well as outside outfits limits. The influencer can choose to gain either Weapon Focus or Armor Focus as a bonus feat.

features.name: Land Owner
features.text:
At 10th level, the influencer has garnered enough prestige to be granted a small plot of land to do with as he pleases. He may choose from: Alchemic Shop, Blacksmith, Church, or Inn. These are stationed within his home town. Once per day, he may use the services of this building, granting him one of the listed effects:
Alchemic Shop: An immediate use of one tier 1 alchemical item, these items cannot be taken away from the store. Alchemical supplies bought from this establishment are 5% cheaper.
Blacksmith: Free repairs of the influencers equipment, or that of one of his companions. He may also select up to 5 weapons to be sharpened, giving them the effects of the whetstone.
Church: A single heal that affects the entire party for 3d6 points of healing, or removing 1 status effect from a single party member, or restoring 3 points of ability damage or drain from 1 ability score, or reviving a party member at a 10% discount for the spellcasting service.
Inn: A free nights rest that grants 2x recovery as if using a sleeping bag. This extends to his adventuring party up to a maximum of 5 people.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: Lil’ witches are skilled with the dagger, power rod, and quarterstaff. Lil’ witches are not proficient with any type of armor or shield. Heavier armor interferes with a lil’ witch’s movements, which can cause her spells with somatic components to fail.

features.name: Spells
features.text:
A lil’ witch casts either black mage spells or white mage spells, which are drawn from the black mage or white mage spell list. On creation, the lil’ witch decides what spell list she will learn. A lil’ witch begins play with 1 1st level spell of her choice. The lil’ witch also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to her Intelligence modifier to add to her list of spells. Each time a character attains a new lil’ witch level, she gains one spell of her choice to add to her list of spells. The free spell must be of spell levels she can cast. Like most mages, a lil’ witch can find or purchase scrolls with spells to add to her repertoire.
To learn or cast a spell, the lil’ witch must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level (Int 11 for 1st-level spells, Int 12 for 2nd-level spells, and so forth). The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a lil’ witch’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the Lil’ witch’s Intelligence modifier. In addition, a lil’ witch gains additional MP for having a high attribute (Intelligence—see Table: Bonus MP per Day (by Spell Level) on the MP System page).
If the lil’ witch selects white mage spells, she uses her Wisdom score instead of Intelligence.

features.name: Cantrips
features.text: Lil’ witches learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume MP and may be used again. Lil’ witches begin with 2 0-level spells and gain an additional 0-level spell every three levels after 1st level.

features.name: Summon Familiar
features.text: At 2nd level, a lil’ witch gains the Familiar feat as a bonus feat.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The malefactor is proficient in the use of dagger, rapier, sap, shortbow, shortsword, and whip. Malefactors are proficient with light armor, but not with any type of shields.

features.name: Hands of the Rogue
features.text: At 3rd level, the malefactor has become quite adept at taking from others, be it from their person or within sight. The malefactor gains a +1 bonus on Steal combat maneuvers and any Stealth or Sleight of Hand skill checks. These bonuses increase by an additional +1 bonus for every 6 levels after 3rd.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The martial arts student is proficient with any light or one-handed weapon with the “monk” special feature as well as weapons from the close warrior weapon group. They are also proficient with light armor and shields (except tower shields).

features.name: Unarmed Proficiency
features.text: At 1st level, a martial arts student gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. A martial arts student may attack with fists, elbows, knees, and feet. This means that a martial arts student may make unarmed strikes with their hands full. A Martial Arts Student applies their full Strength modifier (not half) on damage rolls for all of their unarmed strikes. Usually, a martial arts student’s unarmed strikes deal lethal damage, but they can choose to deal nonlethal damage instead with no penalty on their attack roll. They have the same choice to deal lethal or nonlethal damage while grappling. A martial arts student’s unarmed strike is treated as both a manufactured weapon and a natural weapon for the purpose of spells and effects that modify either manufactured weapons or natural weapons.

features.name: Unarmed Strike
features.text: At 5th level, a martial arts student also deals more damage with their unarmed strikes than others, as shown on the table below. A Small-sized martial arts student deals less damage than a Medium-sized martial arts student with their unarmed attacks, while a Large-sized martial arts student deals more damage; see the following table.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The messenger is proficient with all simple weapons, longbows, and shortbows. Messengers are proficient with light armor, but not with any type of shields.

features.name: Express Mail
features.text: At 1st level, messengers are trained to deliver mail efficiently and quickly, be it with any form of movement. All forms of movement are increased by 5ft, this increases by a further 5ft at every 5th level.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The security guard is proficient with all simple weapons and one simple firearm of his choice (see below) plus tonfas, and with light armor (as well as all tactical armor).

features.name: Gunsmith
features.text:
At 1st level, a security guard gains one of the following firearms of his choice: trainee pistol, trainee rifle or trainee shotgun. His starting weapon is battered, and only he knows how to use it properly. All other creatures treat his gun as if it had the broken condition. If the weapon already has the broken condition, it does not work at all for anyone else trying to use it. This starting weapon can only be sold for scrap (it’s worth 4d10 gil when sold).
At 5th level, the security guard gains Gunsmithing as a bonus feat.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The studious meister is proficient in the use of all simple weapons and with light armor, but not with any type of shields.

features.name: Library Retreat
features.text: The studious meister is adept at using libraries to gain new knowledge as well as being his perfect hobby. The studious meister can make any Knowledge checks as if he was trained. Whenever he selects this class as his favored class bonus, he always gains +1 skill point.

features.name: Focused Study
features.text: At 5th level, the studious meister gains Skill Focus as a bonus feat.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The watchman is proficient in the use of all simple and martial weapons and with all types of armor and shields.

features.name: Guard’s Gear
features.text: At 3rd level, the watchman has his gear upgraded to align with guards of his station, he receives a set of masterwork weapon, armor, and shield, totaling 1,000 gil. If the watchman ever leaves his position or is found to be a criminal, this equipment is forceably taken back. The watchman can otherwise enchant this gear as he pleases and even keeps it when he retires of old age.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: Aetherial tacticians gain no proficiency with any weapon or armor.

features.name: Tactician’s Discipline
features.text:
At 1st level, the aetherial tactician chooses one of two disciplines which dictate how the class enhances their abilities:
• Veteran: This discipline changes all levels of the class to increase BAB by +1, instead of only the 2nd and 4th.
• Wiseman: This discipline changes levels of the class except 1st to grant MP per day and spells known as if the aetherial tactician had also gained a level in a spell-casting class to which he belonged before adding the prestige class level (chosen once this discipline is picked), along with an increased effective level of spellcasting.

features.name: Reaction Tactics
features.text:
At each level of this prestige class, the aetherial tactician gains an available reaction tactic. He may choose one to gain the benefits of at the start of each day and may only benefit from one at a time. As a swift action, he may switch which reaction tactic he benefits from. These abilities only function if opponents and/or hazards are present during combat.
Conditional reaction tactics – these abilities are only usable once per round unless specified otherwise, and require their trigger to be used. Only opponents’ actions can trigger them. They are free actions usable outside of the aetherial tactician’s turn:
• Absorb MP (Su): Trigger: Affected by hostile spell. Effect: After the hostile spell resolves, gain the MP spent on it.
• Adrenaline Rush (Ex): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Movement speed increased by 10ft until end of next turn.
• Auto-Potion (Ex): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Retrieve and drink a potion, even if hands are occupied.
• Bonecrusher (Ex): Trigger: Brought below 10 HP. Effect: Perform an attack of opportunity against an opponent within range but does not count towards limit of attacks of opportunity per round. The attack is an automatic confirmed critical hit.
• Counter (Ex): Trigger: Attacked. Effect: After the attack, perform an attack of opportunity against the attacker. Does not count towards limit of attacks of opportunity per round. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 2.
• Counter Tackle (Ex): Trigger: Targeted with combat maneuver. Effect: Before the opponent’s maneuver, attempt the same maneuver against them without provoking. If your result is higher than the attacker’s, the maneuver is avoided (the effects of your maneuver also apply).
• Critical: Quick (Ex): Trigger: Brought below 10 HP. Effect: Immediately take a standard action. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 3.
• Critical: Recover HP (Ex): Trigger: Brought below 10 HP. Effect: Recover HP equal to Constitution score. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 3.
• Critical: Recover MP (Su): Trigger: Brought below 10 HP. Effect: Recover MP equal to highest mental score modifier. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 3.
• Dragonheart (Su): Trigger: Death. Effect: Immediately recover from death, as if by the Raise spell. If successful, may stand up and retrieve dropped items without provoking. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 4.
• First Strike (Ex): Trigger: Attacked. Effect: Before the attack, perform an attack of opportunity against the attacker. Does not count towards limit of attacks of opportunity per round. Prerequisite: Counter reaction tactic.
• Fury (Ex): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Gain bonus to attack rolls equal to class level until end of next turn.
• Magick Boost (Su): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Gain bonus to caster level equal to his prestige class level until end of next turn.
• Magick Counter (Su): Trigger: Affected by spell. Effect: After the spell resolves, cast a damaging spell of the highest level you know on the opponent who cast the triggering spell.
• Mana Shield (Su): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: The damage is reduced by available MP, at the cost of draining it.
• Nature’s Wrath (Su): Trigger: Attacked, physical. Effect: After the attack, use Geomancy on attacker. Prerequisite: Geomancy class feature.
• Parry (Ex): Trigger: Attacked, melee. Effect: Before the attack, make a melee attack roll. If the result is higher than the attacker’s, the attack is avoided.
• Regenerator (Su): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Gain fast healing 2 for rounds equal to prestige class level. Duration can refresh.
• Soul Bind (Su): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Split damage taken between self and opponent, as if by Shield Other.
• Vanish (Su): Trigger: Attacked. Effect: After the attack, turn invisible for rounds equal to prestige class level. Duration can refresh.
• Vigilance (Ex): Trigger: Damage taken. Effect: Gain +4 dodge bonus to AC until end of next turn.
Passive reaction tactics – these abilities may grant passive effects, but are still reactionary in nature:
• Archer’s Bane (Ex): Gain the Deflect Arrows feat, ignoring prerequisites.
• Cup of Life (Su): When healed above maximum hit points, distribute excess healing to allies within 30 feet. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 2.
• Shirahadori (Ex): Automatically evade the first melee attack made against you each round. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 5.
• Sticky Fingers (Ex): Gain the Snatch Arrows feat, ignoring prerequisites, but cannot throw caught weapons at attackers. Prerequisite: Deflect Arrows feat or Archer’s Bane reaction tactic.

features.name: Support Tactics
features.text:
At 1st, 3rd and 5th levels of this prestige class, the aetherial tactician gains an available support tactic. He may choose one to gain the benefits of at the start of each day and may only benefit from one at a time. As a swift action, he may switch which support tactic he benefits from. These abilities only function if opponents and/or hazards are present during combat. All support tactics are purely passive abilities.
• Arcane Strength (Su): First spell with elemental damage each round deals extra damage equal to his prestige class level.
• Attack Boost (Ex): First melee attack made each round deals extra damage equal to his prestige class level.
• Defense (Su): Gain elemental resistance equal to twice his prestige class level. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 3.
• Defense Boost (Ex): First instance of damage taken each round is reduced by his prestige class level.
• Doublehand (Ex): If wielding a one-handed weapon with two hands, its damage die is increased by two steps.
• Equip Armor (Ex): Gain proficiency with one type of armor (light, medium or heavy) or shields (including tower shields), chosen when the tactic is gained. This tactic may be gained multiple times to designate different types of armor (or shields).
• Equip Weapon (Ex): Gain proficiency with one warrior weapon group, chosen when the tactic is gained. This tactic may be gained multiple times to designate different weapon groups.
• Halve MP (Su): Halves the MP cost of first spell cast each round, rounded down. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 5.
• HP Boost (Su): Maximum hit points increased by his prestige class level times four. These hit points are lost if the ability is swapped out.
• Safeguard (Ex): Worn and carried items cannot be sundered, disarmed or stolen.
• Swiftness (Ex): Gain the improved initiative feat.
• Throw Items (Ex): Gain the Throw Anything feat, and increase the range increment of thrown items by 10 feet.
• Vehemence (Ex): Gain bonus to hit and damage and penalty to AC equal to his prestige class level.

features.name: Movement Tactics
features.text:
At 2nd and 4th levels of this prestige class, the aetherial tactician gains an available movement tactic. He may choose one to gain the benefits of at the start of each day and may only benefit from one at a time. As a swift action, he may switch which movement tactic he benefits from. These abilities only function if opponents and/or hazards are present during combat.
• Float (Su): Gain the Float status effect.
• Fly (Su): Gain a fly speed equal to base movement speed, and ranks in fly skill equal to character level. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 4.
• Ignore Terrain (Ex): Ignore difficult terrain.
• Jump +3 (Ex): Gain +30 bonus on Acrobatics skill checks to jump.
• Lava Walking (Su): Take no damage from heated/burning terrain or fire hazards, and can walk on lava as if solid.
• Lifefont (Su): Once per turn, after moving at least 10 feet, recover HP equal to his prestige class level. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 4.
• Manafont (Su): After your turn ends, if you moved at least 10 feet and spent MP, recover 1 MP. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 4.
• Move +3 (Ex): Increase base movement speed by 15.
• Teleport (Su): When moving in any way, can teleport (without provoking) instead of moving normally. Does not increase movement speed. Prerequisite: Aetherial tactician 4.
• Water Walking (Su): Take no damage or pushback from water hazards, and can walk on water as if solid.

limitBreaks.name: Perfect Tactics
limitBreaks.text: The aetherial tactician gains the benefits of all known tactics for 1 round per aetherial tactician level. His reaction tactics are each usable once per round during this duration. This limit break requires only a swift action.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: Archwizards gain no proficiency with any weapon or armor.

features.name: MP per day / Spells Known
features.text: At each level, an archwizard gains MP per day and spells known as if he had also gained a level in two spell-casting classes (that use different spell lists) to which he belonged before adding the prestige class level and an increased effective level of spellcasting. He does not, however, gain any other benefit a character of these two classes would have gained. If he had more than two spell-casting classes before becoming an archwizard, he must decide to which two classes to add each level for the purpose of determining MP per day and spells known. In addition, if the archwizard has cantrips, he gains a new cantrip at 1st, 5th, and 10th level of this prestige class.

features.name: Superior Casting
features.text: At 1st level, the archwizard chooses one mental ability score (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma) from among those used to determine the Difficulty Class for saving throws against his spells. This ability score is now used to determine the Difficulty Class for saving throws against any of his spells.

features.name: Metamagic Enhancement
features.text: An archwizard is a master at manipulating magical forces. At 1st level, as a move action, he reduces the cost of any metamagic feat known by one MP less than standard. The metamagic enhancement can only reduce 1 metamagic feat at a time. This ability does not affect the Heighten Spell feat. At 5th and 10th level, the adjusted level is reduced one additional MP. The adjusted enhancement can never reduce the base spell below its original level. An archwizard may use this ability up to 3 times per day. This ability does not stack with other metamagic enhancement class features.

features.name: Talented
features.text: At 2nd level and every two archwizard levels thereafter, the archwizard gains a talent from any spellcasting class he has access to using his archwizard level plus the specific spellcasting class as his class level.

features.name: Arcane Servant
features.text: All archwizards of 3rd and higher level are treated as if they have a permanent unseen servant near them at all times. The servant can go no further than 100 ft., but otherwise confer to the rules of normal unseen servants. If destroyed, the servant reappears the following round.

features.name: Detect Expertise
features.text: At 3rd level, an archwizard has a chance of detecting what spellcasting capabilities a creature has. After the archwizard observes a creature with the detect spell for 3 rounds, it must make a Will save (DC 10 + archwizard level + his highest mental stat modifier). If it fails the saving throw, he learns what spells the creature possesses. If the creature makes its save, it is immune to the effects of this ability for 24 hours.

features.name: Spell-Like Ability
features.text: At 5th level, an archwizard can spend MP permanently to have one of his spells as a spell-like ability that can be used twice per day. The MP is permanently removed for the spellcaster’s use. This ability cannot be used with any spell with a material component. The spell-like ability normally uses MP, although the archwizard can choose to make a spell modified by a metamagic feat into a spell-like ability of the appropriate MP cost. This ability may not be combined with the Metamagic Enhancement ability, above.

features.name: Shaped Area
features.text: The 7th level archwizard can alter areas of effect for spells that use one of the following shapes: burst, cone, cylinder, emanation, or spread. The alteration consists of creating spaces within the spell’s area or effect that are not subject to the spell. The minimum dimension for these spaces is a 5 ft. cube. Furthermore, any shapeable spells have a minimum dimension of 5 ft. instead of 10 ft.

features.name: Selective Targets
features.text: At 8th level, the archwizard may select up to one target per point of casting stat bonus to exclude from any area-of-effect spell cast, or double the number of targets affected by a spell. In the first application, the targets are engulfed in the effect, but do not suffer any of the effects. This is a target-based exclusion; other opponents sharing the excluded target’s space are still affected by the spell. In the second case, when a spell description specifies an effect of “one creature/level,” the archwizard may instead affect up to two creatures/level.

features.name: Bypass Spell Resistance
features.text: At 9th level, the archwizard’s command of magic is such that he may unravel a creature’s natural resistance to magic. An archwizard may reduce a target’s spell resistance by his archwizard level, once per day per target for 1 minute. In addition, an archwizard can ignore elemental resistance equal to his combined spellcasting levels for the same duration.

features.name: Archwizardry
features.text: At 10th level, an archwizard is truly the master of magic and its weavings. An archwizard of this level may cast 2 spells with a casting time of “1 standard action” in a single round, one from each of his spellcasting classes. The archwizard may do this 1 time per 6 spellcaster levels per day. This ability does not stack with Quicken Spell or any other ability that increases spells per round.

limitBreaks.name: Spell Perfection
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break allows the archwizard to perfect a spell. For a duration of 1 round + 1 round per two archwizard levels after 1st, the archwizard can cast 1 spell per round without spending MP. This, however, does not work with metamagic feats. This limit break requires only a swift action.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: Blitzers are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with light armor.

features.name: Blitzball Focus
features.text:
At 1st level, the blitzer gains Weapon Focus with either blitzballs or spiked blitzballs at his choice, this cannot be changed later. If the blitzer already has Weapon Focus, he may instead gain Weapon Specialization with the blitzball weapon he has Weapon Focus with. He doesn’t have to meet any of the prerequisites for these feats.
If the blitzer has both Weapon Focus and Weapon Specialization with one of the weapon choices he, instead, may choose a bonus combat feat.

features.name: Returning Ball
features.text:
At 1st level, a blitzer can kick a blitzball so it ricochets off his target (and possibly other solid objects) to return to him at the end of his turn. This ability functions whether or not the blitzer hits his opponent or moves on his turn. The blitzball deals no damage to targets it bounces off other than the original target of the blitzer’s attack. Other circumstances can prevent the blitzball from returning to the blitzer, such as an opponent using a readied action to catch the blitzball, or the blitzball sticking to a mimic’s adhesive. The blitzer can opt to not have a blitzball return to him, in which case it falls to the ground as it normally would. If the blitzball has the returning weapon special ability, he can use either that or this ability.
If a blitzer has additional attacks from a high base attack bonus, these additional attacks can be ricochets off an earlier target. The distance to each additional target adds to the total range of the blitzball, and range penalties apply, but there are no additional penalties for attacking in this manner. Because ricocheting attacks are treated as separate attacks, effects and modifiers that only apply to one attack roll (such as true strike) only apply to the first attack and not to the others.
At 5th level, by ricocheting his blitzball off a nearby surface before hitting his intended target, he can treat that surface as the origin square of the attack to determine whether the target is flanked and whether the target gains a cover bonus to its AC. He can use this ability to attack a creature with total concealment from him if he knows what square it occupies, but the attack still has a 50% miss chance.

features.name: Stamina Pool
features.text:
At 1st level, the blitzer gains a reservoir of stamina that he can draw upon to fuel his talents that he gains below. This stamina pool has a number of points equal to his blitzer level + his Constitution modifier (minimum 1). The pool refreshes once per day when the blitzer rests for a full 8 hours. Sustained modes take up a static amount of stamina points from the blitzer’s current and maximum stamina pool and most sustained modes stack.
By spending 1 stamina point as a swift action, the blitzer can do one of the following:
• Increase his speed by 10 feet for 1 round, or
• Delay and suppress his fatigue or exhaustion for 1 round, or
• Increase one saving throw by +1 for 1 round.

features.name: Blitzer Talent Tree
features.text:
As a blitzer gains experience, he learns a number of talents that aid him and his allies. Starting at 1st level, a blitzer gains one blitzer talent chosen from the talent tree below. He gains an additional blitzer talent for every blitzer level attained after 1st level. A blitzer cannot select an individual talent more than once.
• Quick Hit (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, as part of a full attack, a blitzer can make one additional attack with his blitzball. This attack is at the blitzer’s highest base attack bonus, but each attack in the round (including the extra one) takes a –2 penalty.
• Dark Attack (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with blinding magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted with the Blind status effect for 1d4 rounds.
• Silence Attack (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with anti-magic magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Will save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted with the Silence status effect and be unable to cast spells or use spell-like abilities for 1d4 rounds.
• Sleep Attack (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with sleep magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Will save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted by the Sleep status effect and fall unconscious for 1d4 rounds.
• Delay Attack (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack with even more vigor. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be stunned for 1 round.
• Dark Buster (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with more powerful magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted with permanent blindness. Prerequisite: Dark Attack
• Silence Buster (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with more powerful magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Will save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted with the Silence status effect and be unable to cast spells or use spell-like abilities for 3d4 rounds. Prerequisite: Silence Attack
• Sleep Buster (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with more powerful magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must succeed a Will save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted by the Sleep status effect and fall unconscious for 3d4 rounds. Prerequisite: Sleep Attack
• Delay Buster (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with more powerful magic. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be stunned for 1d4 rounds. Prerequisite: Delay Attack
• Power Dampen (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that saps the enemy’s Strength. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or take 1d4 points of Strength damage.
• Magic Dampen (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that saps the enemy’s Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (decided when the blitzer makes the attack roll). If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or take 1d4 points of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma damage.
• Speed Dampen (Su): At a cost of 1 stamina point, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that saps the enemy’s speed. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or have their movement speed halved for 1d4 rounds.
• Power Break (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that greatly saps the enemy’s Strength. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or take 3d4 points of Strength damage. Prerequisites: Blitzer 6, Power Dampen
• Magic Break (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that greatly saps the enemy’s Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (decided when the blitzer makes the attack roll). If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or take 3d4 points of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma damage. Prerequisites: Blitzer 6, Magic Dampen
• Speed Break (Su): At a cost of 2 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that greatly saps the enemy’s speed. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) or be inflicted with Immobilize status effect for 3d4 rounds. Prerequisites: Blitzer 6, Speed Dampen
• Triple Foul (Su): At a cost of 3 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack enchanted with more powerful magic, applying Dark Buster, Silence Buster, and Sleep Buster. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude or Will save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) for each buster or suffer the effects. Prerequisites: Dark Buster, Silence Buster, Sleep Buster
• Full Break (Su): At a cost of 3 stamina points, the blitzer launches a blitzball attack that greatly saps the enemy, applying Power Break, Magic Break, and Speed Break. If struck, the target takes damage as normal and must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) for each break or suffer the effects. Prerequisites: Power Break, Magic Break, Speed Break

features.name: Golden Arm
features.text: At 2nd level and every two levels thereafter, the blitzer gains a +1 to attack and damage rolls with a blitzball. Additionally, a blitzer only suffers a -2 to attack rolls per range increment rather than -4 while using a blitzball underwater.

features.name: Frontliner Blitzer
features.text: At 3rd level, the blitzer gains Point-Blank Shot as a bonus feat. If the blitzer already has Point-Blank Shot he, instead, gains Precise Shot, or Improved Precise Shot if he already has Precise Shot. He doesn’t have to meet any of the prerequisites for these feats. If the blitzer has these feats already he, instead, may choose a bonus combat feat.

features.name: Safe Throw
features.text: At 5th level, the blitzer can throw his blitzball without provoking attacks of opportunity.

features.name: Critical Shot
features.text: At 7th level, the blitzer knows where to hit with his blitzball to bring down an opponent. The critical threat range and multiplier of the blitzball is increased by 1 (applied after Improved Critical).

features.name: World Champion
features.text: At 10th level, the blitzer is superb on the on the field. In the hands of the blitzer, the blitzball deals damage as if it were two die step higher.

limitBreaks.name: Line Breaker
limitBreaks.text: This Limit Break allows the blitzer to kick his blitzball in a 60-ft.-line. All enemies within the area of effect take damage as if the blitzer hit with a blitzball attack plus an additional 1d6 points of damage per blitzer level and are knocked prone. A successful Reflex save (DC 10 + the blitzer’s level + his Dexterity modifier) reduces the damage by half and avoids being knocked prone. The blitzball returns to the blitzer immediately at the end of this Limit Break.

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.text: The clan hunter is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with light armor. In addition, the clan hunter is proficient in the Mancatcher, Bolas, Lassos and Nets (including Snag Nets).

features.name: Clan’s Mark
features.text:
A clan hunter can target, or mark, an individual humanoid or monstrous humanoid foe to better hunt that enemy. To do so, the clan hunter must focus on a foe that is present and visible, or on the depiction or description of the creature, for 10 minutes. Any interruption ruins the attempt and forces the clan hunter to start the process again. Once this study is complete, that target is called a mark. A clan hunter adds his clan hunter level as an insight bonus on all Diplomacy, Perception, and Survival checks made to determine the whereabouts of a mark. As a clan hunter gains levels, he gains additional abilities against a mark. A clan hunter can choose a mark only once a week.
Initially, a clan hunter can have only one mark at a time. For every three clan hunter levels gained beyond the 1st, a clan hunter can have one additional mark, but only if all the marks are chosen during the same process (see above). If a clan hunter gives up on finishing any of his marks, all remaining marked creatures become unmarked as described above.

features.name: Track
features.text: At 1st level, a clan hunter adds his clan hunter level to Survival skill checks made to follow or identify tracks.

features.name: Quarry
features.text:
At 1st level, a clan hunter’s most well-known ability is tracking creatures: detecting them, locating them, identifying them, and observing important details about them. These abilities come with the limitation that the clan hunter must concentrate his attention on the target in order to do these things properly. So, the clan hunter learns to focus his concentration and attention on one creature: his quarry.
To make a creature his quarry, the clan hunter must take a moment to gather his thoughts and visualize the creature in his mind. This means the clan hunter must know enough about the creature to identify and describe them. Once per round as a free action, the clan hunter can make anyone he remembers encountering and interacting with in for at least 10 minutes in the past 24 hours his quarry. If a clan hunter is extremely familiar with someone, he can make them his quarry up to 1 year after encountering them. This includes anyone he has spent an extended period of time interacting with (at least 2 hours total). Even if the creature is not present, the clan hunter can make them his quarry.
If the clan hunter meets a creature, he can study it so that he makes it his quarry immediately. A clan hunter can make any creature his quarry if he can see them (or sense in a unique way, such as by using a form of blindsense) as a move action.
Finally, a clan hunter can also make a creature his quarry based on evidence of their presence, without even knowing exactly who they are. If a clan hunter makes a successful Survival or Perception skill check to find tracks or other signs of a creature’s passage, he may make that creature his quarry as a standard action. If the clan hunter fails, he may not try to quarry that creature again for 24 hours, unless he discovers tracks or other signs of passage at a different, unrelated location.
A clan hunter has several special abilities that relate to his quarry:
• A clan hunter is skilled in finding his quarry. When making Survival skill checks made to follow his quarry’s tracks, the clan hunter adds his clan hunter level to his check and can move at his normal speed while using following tracks without taking the normal –5 penalty. He takes only a –10 penalty (instead of the normal –20) when moving at up to twice normal speed while tracking.
• When making Perception skill checks to locate his quarry (such as if the quarry is invisible or hiding), to confirm their identity (such as if the quarry is disguised), or to determine if something belongs to the quarry or was left behind by them, the clan hunter adds his clan hunter level to his check.
• A clan hunter may attempt to use a Knowledge check to identify the creature type of his quarry based on its tracks or evidence of their passage.
• A clan hunter may make a Perception skill check against his quarry’s Disguise or Bluff check (whichever is higher) to gain some information about its condition at the time they were present, just by looking at the quarry’s tracks. They may learn the following: whether the creature was badly injured (has less than half of its hit points), whether it had any conditions that affect its movement (such as blindness or a missing leg), or whether it was encumbered. The clan hunter can also tell whether the quarry was running or walking.
A quarry lasts until the clan hunter chooses a different quarry. For the purpose of this ability, a troop or swarm is considered a single creature.

features.name: Woodland Stride
features.text: Starting at 2nd level, a clan hunter may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at his normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment.

features.name: Ready and Waiting
features.text: Beginning at 2nd level, a clan hunter is ready for trickery at all times. He can ready an action against his mark, even outside of the initiative sequence. If the mark triggers the clan hunter’s readied action at any point within the next 10 minutes, the clan hunter can carry out his readied action as if the two were engaged in combat (as long as the clan hunter is capable of carrying out that action. If the clan hunter is incapable of carrying out the action—for instance, if he is too far away to strike the mark with a readied melee attack—the readied action is lost.

features.name: Improved Quarry
features.text:
As a clan hunter becomes more skilled at hunting, he learns to make creatures his quarry with greater efficiency.
• Charging Focus: At 2nd level, the clan hunter may quarry a creature as a move action and move towards that creature (or direct his mount to move towards that creature) as part of the same move action. He may quarry as part of a charge.
• Sudden Focus: At 4th level, the clan hunter may quarry a creature he can see as a swift action.
